text: Complete JavaScript Notes Page 1 COMPLETE JAVASCRIPT NOTES Beginner to Intermediate • Simple explanations • Examples • Outputs • Interview points How to use these notes: Read one topic, type the examples yourself, predict the output before running the code, and then practise the questions at the end. Topics included G JavaScript basics, variables, data types and operators G Conditions, loops, functions, arrays and objects G Strings, scope, hoisting, closures and the this keyword G DOM, events, browser storage and error handling G Modern JavaScript (ES6+), promises and async/await G Common interview questions and practice exercises

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 2 1. Introduction to JavaScript Definition: JavaScript is a programming language used to make websites interactive and dynamic. It can also run outside the browser using environments such as Node.js. Technology Main purpose HTML Creates the structure/content of a webpage. CSS Controls the appearance and layout. JavaScript Adds behaviour and interactivity. Examples of what JavaScript can do G Respond when a user clicks a button. G Validate a login or signup form. G Show, hide or update webpage content. G Fetch information from a server. G Build web servers and command-line tools with Node.js. Adding JavaScript to HTML Inline: JavaScript is written in an HTML attribute. Useful for tiny demonstrations, but usually avoid it in larger projects. <button onclick="alert('Hello!')">Click me</button> Internal: JavaScript is written inside a script element. <script> console.log("Hello, JavaScript!"); </script> External: JavaScript is stored in a separate .js file. This is usually the cleanest

projects. <button onclick="alert('Hello!')">Click me</button> Internal: JavaScript is written inside a script element. <script> console.log("Hello, JavaScript!"); </script> External: JavaScript is stored in a separate .js file. This is usually the cleanest approach. <!-- index.html --> <script src="script.js" defer></script> // script.js console.log("Hello from an external file"); Tip: The defer attribute downloads the script while HTML is being parsed and runs it after the document has been parsed. 2. Variables: var, let and const Definition: A variable is a named place used by a program to refer to a value. var city = "Mumbai"; let age = 21; const country = "India"; Feature var let const Can be redeclared in the same scope? Yes No No Can be reassigned? Yes Yes No Scope Function/global Block Block

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 3 Feature var let const Must have a value at declaration? No No Yes Examples let score = 10; score = 20; // allowed const pi = 3.14; // pi = 4; // TypeError: reassignment is not allowed const user = { name: "Asha" }; user.name = "Riya"; // allowed: object property is changed Use const by default. Use let when you need to reassign. Avoid var in modern code unless you have a specific reason. Important: const prevents assigning a new value to the variable. It does not make an object or array deeply immutable. 3. Data Types A data type describes the kind of value being used. JavaScript has primitive types and object types. Primitive types Type Meaning Example Number Integers and decimal numbers let price = 99.5; String Text let name = "Asha"; Boolean true or false let isReady = true; Undefined A

Primitive types Type Meaning Example Number Integers and decimal numbers let price = 99.5; String Text let name = "Asha"; Boolean true or false let isReady = true; Undefined A declared variable with no assigned value let result; Null An intentional absence of a value let selected = null; BigInt Very large integers let big = 123n; Symbol A unique identifier let id = Symbol("id"); Object types Objects store properties, arrays store ordered collections, and functions are callable objects. const student = { name: "Asha", age: 21 }; const marks = [80, 90, 95]; function greet() { console.log("Hello"); } typeof operator typeof returns a string describing the type of a value. console.log(typeof 42); // "number" console.log(typeof "hi"); // "string" console.log(typeof true); // "boolean" console.log(typeof undefined); // "undefined" console.log(typeof {}); // "object" console.log(typeof null); // "object" (historic JavaScript quirk) console.log(typeof function(){}); // "function"

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 4 Remember: null is a primitive value even though typeof null returns "object". This is a long-standing historical behaviour. 4. Type Conversion and Coercion Type conversion means deliberately changing a value from one type to another. Type coercion is conversion JavaScript performs automatically in some operations. // Explicit conversion Number("25"); // 25 String(25); // "25" Boolean(1); // true parseInt("42px"); // 42 parseFloat("3.5"); // 3.5 // Automatic coercion console.log("5" + 2); // "52" (string concatenation) console.log("5" - 2); // 3 (numeric conversion) Truthy and falsy values In a condition, JavaScript treats values as truthy or falsy. The main falsy values are: false, 0, -0, 0n, empty string (""), null, undefined and NaN. Almost everything else is truthy, including empty arrays and empty objects. if ([]) { console.log("This runs: an empty array is truthy"); } 5. Operators Category Operators / purpose Arithmetic + - * / % **

including empty arrays and empty objects. if ([]) { console.log("This runs: an empty array is truthy"); } 5. Operators Category Operators / purpose Arithmetic + - * / % ** ++ -- Assignment = += -= *= /= %= Comparison == === != !== > < >= <= Logical && (AND), || (OR), ! (NOT) Nullish coalescing ?? uses the right side only for null or undefined Ternary condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse Type typeof, instanceof Equality: == versus === console.log(10 == "10"); // true: values are compared after coercion console.log(10 === "10"); // false: types are different Prefer === and !== because they avoid unexpected type conversion. Logical operators const age = 22; const hasID = true; console.log(age >= 18 && hasID); // true console.log(age < 18 || hasID); // true console.log(!hasID); // false

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 5 Ternary operator const age = 17; const status = age >= 18 ? "Adult" : "Minor"; console.log(status); // "Minor" Nullish coalescing and optional chaining const input = null; const name = input ?? "Guest"; // "Guest" const user = {}; console.log(user.address?.city); // undefined, no error 6. Conditional Statements Conditions let a program choose which code to execute. const marks = 82; if (marks >= 90) { console.log("Grade A"); } else if (marks >= 75) { console.log("Grade B"); } else { console.log("Keep practising"); } switch Use switch when one expression is compared with several possible values. const day = 2; switch (day) { case 1: console.log("Monday"); break; case 2: console.log("Tuesday"); break; default: console.log("Unknown day"); } Why break? It prevents execution from continuing into the next case. Without break, switch can fall through. 7. Loops Loops repeat a block of code while a condition or iteration rule

break? It prevents execution from continuing into the next case. Without break, switch can fall through. 7. Loops Loops repeat a block of code while a condition or iteration rule allows it. for loop for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { console.log(i); } // 1, 2, 3 while loop

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 6 let i = 1; while (i <= 3) { console.log(i); i++; } do...while loop A do...while loop runs its body at least once because it checks the condition afterwards. let count = 5; do { console.log(count); } while (count < 3); // prints 5 once for...of and for...in const colors = ["red", "blue"]; for (const color of colors) { console.log(color); // values } const person = { name: "Asha", age: 21 }; for (const key in person) { console.log(key, person[key]); // property keys and values } Loop Best used for for Repeating with a counter or known iteration pattern. while Repeating while a condition remains true. do...while When the body must run at least once. for...of Reading values from an iterable such as an array or string. for...in Enumerating an object's property keys. 8. Functions Definition: A function is a reusable block of code that

for...of Reading values from an iterable such as an array or string. for...in Enumerating an object's property keys. 8. Functions Definition: A function is a reusable block of code that performs a task. Function declaration function greet() { console.log("Hello!"); } greet(); Parameters, arguments and return function add(a, b) { // a and b are parameters return a + b; } const total = add(10, 20); // 10 and 20 are arguments console.log(total); // 30 console.log() displays a value. return sends a value back to the caller and ends that function call. Function expression

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 7 const sayHi = function() { console.log("Hi!"); }; sayHi(); Arrow function const multiply = (a, b) => a * b; console.log(multiply(4, 5)); // 20 An arrow function with one parameter can omit parentheses: x => x * 2. Arrow functions do not have their own this or arguments binding. Callback and higher-order function A callback is a function passed to another function. A higher-order function accepts a function as an argument or returns a function. function processNumber(value, callback) { return callback(value); } const doubled = processNumber(5, n => n * 2); console.log(doubled); // 10 IIFE An Immediately Invoked Function Expression runs as soon as it is created. (function() { console.log("Runs immediately"); })(); Default parameters and rest parameters function welcome(name = "Guest") { console.log("Hello " + name); } welcome(); // Hello Guest function sum(...numbers) { return numbers.reduce((total, n) => total + n, 0); } console.log(sum(1, 2, 3));

parameters function welcome(name = "Guest") { console.log("Hello " + name); } welcome(); // Hello Guest function sum(...numbers) { return numbers.reduce((total, n) => total + n, 0); } console.log(sum(1, 2, 3)); // 6 9. Arrays An array stores an ordered list of values. Array indexes start at 0. const fruits = ["Apple", "Mango", "Banana"]; console.log(fruits[0]); // Apple console.log(fruits.length); // 3 Method What it does Example push(x) Adds to the end arr.push(40) pop() Removes from the end arr.pop() unshift(x) Adds to the beginning arr.unshift(5)

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 8 Method What it does Example shift() Removes from the beginning arr.shift() includes(x) Checks whether a value exists arr.includes(20) indexOf(x) Returns first matching index, or -1 arr.indexOf(20) slice(a,b) Returns a shallow portion; end excluded arr.slice(1,3) splice(a,n) Changes original array by removing n items at a arr.splice(1,2) join(sep) Joins elements into a string arr.join(", ") concat(other) Returns a combined array arr.concat(other) slice versus splice const values = [10, 20, 30, 40]; const part = values.slice(1, 3); console.log(part); // [20, 30] console.log(values); // original unchanged values.splice(1, 2); console.log(values); // [10, 40] (original changed) map, filter, forEach and reduce map() returns a new array containing the result of transforming each element. const nums = [1, 2, 3]; const doubled = nums.map(num => num * 2); console.log(doubled); // [2, 4, 6] Here, num is simply the callback parameter. During each call it represents the current array element. filter() returns a

= nums.map(num => num * 2); console.log(doubled); // [2, 4, 6] Here, num is simply the callback parameter. During each call it represents the current array element. filter() returns a new array containing only elements that pass a test. const nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; const evens = nums.filter(num => num % 2 === 0); console.log(evens); // [2, 4] forEach() runs a callback for each element. It returns undefined, so it is not used to build a transformed array. ["a", "b"].forEach(item => console.log(item)); reduce() combines array values into one result, such as a sum. const nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]; const total = nums.reduce((sum, num) => sum + num, 0); console.log(total); // 10 Method Returns Common purpose map() New array Transform every element. filter() New array Keep matching elements. forEach() undefined Perform an action for each element. reduce() One accumulated result Sum, count, group or combine values.

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 9 sort const nums = [10, 2, 30]; nums.sort((a, b) => a - b); // ascending numeric order console.log(nums); // [2, 10, 30] Note: sort() changes the original array. Without a comparator, values are sorted as strings. 10. Strings A string is text surrounded by single quotes, double quotes or backticks. const first = "Java"; const second = 'Script'; const language = `${first}${second}`; console.log(language); // JavaScript Property / method Purpose length Number of characters. toUpperCase() Returns uppercase text. toLowerCase() Returns lowercase text. trim() Removes whitespace from both ends. includes(text) Checks whether text occurs inside. startsWith(text) Checks the beginning. endsWith(text) Checks the ending. indexOf(text) Finds the first position. slice(start,end) Extracts part of a string; end excluded. replace(a,b) Replaces the first matching occurrence (or matches with a global regex). split(separator) Splits a string into an array. const message = " Learn JavaScript "; console.log(message.trim()); // "Learn JavaScript" console.log(message.toUpperCase());

Replaces the first matching occurrence (or matches with a global regex). split(separator) Splits a string into an array. const message = " Learn JavaScript "; console.log(message.trim()); // "Learn JavaScript" console.log(message.toUpperCase()); // " LEARN JAVASCRIPT " console.log("a,b,c".split(",")); // ["a", "b", "c"] console.log("Hello".includes("ell")); // true Strings are immutable: string methods return a new string rather than changing the original string. 11. Objects An object stores related information as key-value pairs. A key is also called a property name.

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 10 const student = { name: "Asha", age: 21, greet: function() { console.log("Hello!"); } }; console.log(student.name); // dot notation console.log(student["age"]); // bracket notation student.city = "Mumbai"; // add property delete student.age; // remove property student.greet(); Object utilities const person = { name: "Asha", age: 21 }; console.log(Object.keys(person)); // ["name", "age"] console.log(Object.values(person)); // ["Asha", 21] console.log(Object.entries(person)); // [["name","Asha"],["age",21]] Destructuring const user = { name: "Riya", age: 20 }; const { name, age } = user; const colors = ["red", "blue"]; const [firstColor, secondColor] = colors; Spread syntax const oldArray = [1, 2]; const newArray = [...oldArray, 3]; // [1, 2, 3] const oldUser = { name: "Asha" }; const newUser = { ...oldUser, city: "Pune" }; Spread makes a shallow copy. Nested objects are still shared unless they are copied separately. 12. Scope, Hoisting and Closures Scope Scope decides where a variable can be accessed. const globalName

makes a shallow copy. Nested objects are still shared unless they are copied separately. 12. Scope, Hoisting and Closures Scope Scope decides where a variable can be accessed. const globalName = "Asha"; function show() { const localName = "Riya"; console.log(globalName); // accessible console.log(localName); // accessible here } show(); // console.log(localName); // ReferenceError G Global scope: accessible in the relevant global environment. G Function scope: available inside the function. G Block scope: let and const are limited to the surrounding { } block.

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 11 Hoisting Hoisting describes how JavaScript processes declarations before executing code. It does not mean every variable can safely be used before its declaration. console.log(a); // undefined var a = 10; // console.log(b); // ReferenceError (temporal dead zone) let b = 20; sayHello(); // works function sayHello() { console.log("Hello"); } Closure A closure happens when a function remembers and can access variables from the scope where it was created, even after that outer function has finished. function makeCounter() { let count = 0; return function() { count++; return count; }; } const counter = makeCounter(); console.log(counter()); // 1 console.log(counter()); // 2 13. this Keyword and Classes The value of this depends on how a function is called. In a method call, this usually refers to the object before the dot. Arrow functions do not create their own this. const user = { name: "Asha", showName() {

called. In a method call, this usually refers to the object before the dot. Arrow functions do not create their own this. const user = { name: "Asha", showName() { console.log(this.name); } }; user.showName(); // Asha Classes A class is a syntax for creating objects with shared structure and behaviour. JavaScript classes use prototypes underneath. class Person { constructor(name) { this.name = name; } greet() { return `Hello, ${this.name}`; } } const person = new Person("Asha"); console.log(person.greet()); // Hello, Asha

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 12 Inheritance class Animal { speak() { console.log("Animal sound"); } } class Dog extends Animal { bark() { console.log("Woof!"); } } const dog = new Dog(); dog.speak(); dog.bark(); 14. DOM (Document Object Model) The DOM is the browser's object representation of an HTML document. JavaScript can use it to read and change page content, styles and elements. // Find elements const title = document.getElementById("title"); const item = document.querySelector(".item"); // Change content title.textContent = "Welcome"; // Change style title.style.color = "blue"; // Create and add an element const para = document.createElement("p"); para.textContent = "A new paragraph"; document.body.appendChild(para); Method / property Purpose getElementById() Find an element by its id. querySelector() Find the first element matching a CSS selector. querySelectorAll() Find all matching elements. textContent Read or set text content. innerHTML Read or set HTML markup; be careful with untrusted input. classList.add/remove/toggle() Change CSS classes. createElement() Create a new

querySelectorAll() Find all matching elements. textContent Read or set text content. innerHTML Read or set HTML markup; be careful with untrusted input. classList.add/remove/toggle() Change CSS classes. createElement() Create a new element. appendChild() Add a child node. Security tip: Prefer textContent for untrusted text. Assigning untrusted content to innerHTML can create cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities. 15. Events An event is an action or occurrence in the browser, such as a click, key press, form submission or page load.

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 13 const button = document.querySelector("#save"); button.addEventListener("click", function() { console.log("Button clicked!"); }); Common events G click — user clicks an element. G input — a form control's value changes. G change — a value is committed/changed. G submit — a form is submitted. G keydown — a key is pressed. G mouseover — pointer moves onto an element. Event object button.addEventListener("click", function(event) { console.log(event.type); console.log(event.target); }); Prevent default behaviour const form = document.querySelector("form"); form.addEventListener("submit", function(event) { event.preventDefault(); // stops normal form navigation console.log("Handle form data here"); }); Event bubbling In event bubbling, an event starts at the target element and then travels up through its ancestors. Event delegation uses this to handle events from many child elements with one listener on a parent. 16. Asynchronous JavaScript JavaScript often needs to wait for work such as a timer or a network request. Asynchronous code lets the program continue

with one listener on a parent. 16. Asynchronous JavaScript JavaScript often needs to wait for work such as a timer or a network request. Asynchronous code lets the program continue instead of blocking while that work completes. setTimeout and setInterval setTimeout(() => { console.log("Runs once after about 1 second"); }, 1000); const id = setInterval(() => { console.log("Runs repeatedly"); }, 1000); // Stop it when no longer needed: clearInterval(id); Promise A Promise represents the eventual success or failure of an asynchronous operation. Its states are pending, fulfilled or rejected.

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 14 const promise = new Promise((resolve, reject) => { const success = true; if (success) { resolve("Work completed"); } else { reject(new Error("Something failed")); } }); promise .then(result => console.log(result)) .catch(error => console.error(error)) .finally(() => console.log("Finished")); async and await An async function always returns a Promise. await pauses that async function until the awaited Promise settles; it does not block the entire JavaScript thread. async function loadData() { try { const response = await fetch("https://example.com/data"); if (!response.ok) { throw new Error("Request failed"); } const data = await response.json(); console.log(data); } catch (error) { console.error(error); } } loadData(); Event loop: simple idea JavaScript runs synchronous code on the call stack. Browser/Node features handle certain asynchronous work. When work is ready, callbacks are queued; the event loop schedules them when the stack is clear. Promise callbacks (microtasks) are generally processed before timer callbacks (tasks/macrotasks). console.log("A"); setTimeout(() => console.log("B"),

work is ready, callbacks are queued; the event loop schedules them when the stack is clear. Promise callbacks (microtasks) are generally processed before timer callbacks (tasks/macrotasks). console.log("A"); setTimeout(() => console.log("B"), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("C")); console.log("D"); // Output: A, D, C, B 17. JSON, Fetch and Web Storage JSON JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a text format commonly used to exchange data. const user = { name: "Asha", age: 21 }; const jsonText = JSON.stringify(user); // object -> JSON string const backToObject = JSON.parse(jsonText); // JSON string -> object Fetch API

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 15 fetch() makes a network request and returns a Promise. Check response.ok because HTTP error statuses do not automatically reject the Promise. fetch("https://example.com/users") .then(response => { if (!response.ok) throw new Error("HTTP error"); return response.json(); }) .then(data => console.log(data)) .catch(error => console.error(error)); localStorage and sessionStorage Storage How long it lasts localStorage Persists across browser restarts until cleared. sessionStorage Usually lasts for the lifetime of the browser tab session. localStorage.setItem("theme", "dark"); const theme = localStorage.getItem("theme"); localStorage.removeItem("theme"); // Store objects as JSON: localStorage.setItem("user", JSON.stringify({ name: "Asha" })); const user = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("user")); Web Storage stores strings. Do not store passwords, secret tokens or sensitive information in it without understanding the security risks. 18. Error Handling and Regular Expressions try, catch and finally try { const data = JSON.parse("{invalid json}"); console.log(data); } catch (error) { console.log("Could not parse JSON"); } finally { console.log("This runs either way"); } Use throw to create

and finally try { const data = JSON.parse("{invalid json}"); console.log(data); } catch (error) { console.log("Could not parse JSON"); } finally { console.log("This runs either way"); } Use throw to create an error when an operation cannot continue as expected. function divide(a, b) { if (b === 0) { throw new Error("Cannot divide by zero"); } return a / b; } Regular expressions (RegExp) A regular expression is a pattern used to search, match or replace text. const text = "My number is 9876543210"; const digits = text.match(/\d+/g); console.log(digits); // ["9876543210"] console.log(/hello/i.test("Hello")); // true

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 16 Pattern Meaning \d A digit from 0 to 9. \w A word character (letters, digits or underscore). \s Whitespace. + One or more of the preceding item. * Zero or more. ^ Beginning of input. $ End of input. [abc] Any one of a, b or c. 19. Important ES6+ Features Feature Simple meaning let and const Block-scoped variable declarations. Arrow functions Short function syntax; lexical this. Template literals Backticks allow interpolation and multiline strings. Destructuring Extract values from arrays or properties from objects. Spread syntax Expand iterable values or object properties. Rest parameters Collect remaining arguments into an array. Default parameters Use a fallback when an argument is undefined. Modules Share code using export and import. Optional chaining Safely access a nested property. Nullish coalescing Fallback only for null or undefined. Modules // math.js export function add(a, b) { return a + b; }

and import. Optional chaining Safely access a nested property. Nullish coalescing Fallback only for null or undefined. Modules // math.js export function add(a, b) { return a + b; } // app.js import { add } from "./math.js"; console.log(add(2, 3)); // 5 In a browser, use a module script: <script type="module" src="app.js"></script>. 20. Imperative vs Declarative Programming Imperative Declarative Explains HOW to do a task. Explains WHAT result is wanted. Describes steps and control flow. Describes the desired outcome. Often uses loops and assignments. Often uses methods or queries.

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 17 Imperative example: const nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]; const evens = []; for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) { if (nums[i] % 2 === 0) { evens.push(nums[i]); } } Declarative example: const nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]; const evens = nums.filter(num => num % 2 === 0); Both produce [2, 4]. In the second example, filter describes the result wanted; JavaScript handles the iteration details. 21. Common Interview Questions What is JavaScript? A programming language used to add behaviour to webpages and to build applications in other environments. Is JavaScript compiled or interpreted? Modern engines commonly use multiple techniques, including interpretation and just-in-time compilation. It is not useful to describe all JavaScript execution as only one or the other. Is JavaScript statically or dynamically typed? Dynamically typed: a variable can refer to values of different types at different times. What

all JavaScript execution as only one or the other. Is JavaScript statically or dynamically typed? Dynamically typed: a variable can refer to values of different types at different times. What is NaN? A special Number value meaning Not-a-Number. Use Number.isNaN() to test it reliably. What is the difference between null and undefined? undefined commonly means no value has been assigned; null is an intentional empty value. What is the difference between == and ===? == allows type coercion; === compares without coercion. What is the difference between map and forEach? map returns a new array; forEach runs a callback and returns undefined. What is the difference between filter and find? filter returns all matching elements in an array; find returns the first matching element or undefined. What is the DOM? The browser's object representation of an HTML document. What is a callback? A function passed to another function to be

the first matching element or undefined. What is the DOM? The browser's object representation of an HTML document. What is a callback? A function passed to another function to be called later or during its work. What is a Promise? An object representing the eventual result of an asynchronous operation. What does async do? It makes a function return a Promise. What does await do? It waits for a Promise inside an async function and resumes that function when it settles. What is a closure? A function retaining access to variables from its outer lexical scope. What is hoisting? JavaScript's declaration-processing behaviour before code execution; var, let, const and function declarations behave

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 18 differently. What is event bubbling? An event travels from its target element up through ancestor elements. What is the difference between localStorage and sessionStorage? localStorage persists until cleared; sessionStorage is scoped to a tab's session. What is the difference between slice and splice? slice returns a portion without changing the original; splice changes the original array. What is typeof null? It is "object" due to a historical JavaScript quirk, although null is primitive. What is the difference between function and arrow function? Arrow functions have lexical this and no own arguments; regular functions have their own this depending on the call. 22. Practice Questions Try solving these without looking at the answers first. G Write a function that returns the square of a number. G Count the even numbers in an array. G Find the largest number in an array. G Reverse a string. G

a function that returns the square of a number. G Count the even numbers in an array. G Find the largest number in an array. G Reverse a string. G Check whether a number is a palindrome. G Use map() to convert an array of prices from rupees to paise. G Use filter() to keep numbers greater than 10. G Use reduce() to calculate the sum of an array. G Create an object for a student and print each key and value. G Add a click event listener to a button that changes a heading. Sample solutions // 1. Square const square = n => n * n; // 2. Count even numbers const countEvens = arr => arr.filter(n => n % 2 === 0).length; // 3. Largest number const largest = arr => Math.max(...arr); // 4. Reverse a string const reverse = str => str.split("").reverse().join(""); // 7. Values greater

n % 2 === 0).length; // 3. Largest number const largest = arr => Math.max(...arr); // 4. Reverse a string const reverse = str => str.split("").reverse().join(""); // 7. Values greater than 10 const greaterThanTen = arr => arr.filter(n => n > 10); // 8. Sum const sumArray = arr => arr.reduce((sum, n) => sum + n, 0); 23. Quick Revision Sheet Concept Remember Variable A named reference to a value.

Complete JavaScript Notes Page 19 Concept Remember Primitive A simple value such as number, string or boolean. Array An ordered collection; indexes start at zero. Object A collection of key-value properties. Function Reusable code that can be called. Callback A function passed to another function. Closure A function remembers its outer lexical variables. DOM The browser's object representation of a page. Event An action such as click, input or submit. Promise Represents a future asynchronous result. async/await Syntax for working with Promises. map Transform each array element into a new array. filter Keep array elements that pass a test. reduce Combine array values into one result. Declarative Describe what result you want. Imperative Describe the steps to get the result. Best way to learn: Do not only read examples.
